title: Logical Comms: subscriptions are wiring; direct queues carry communications
summary: The logical Comms layer separates authorised subscription/wiring state from actual messages. Subscription selects definitions, observation plans and journey preparation; direct queue delivery carries live semantic communications and events.
invariants: Subscription is authorised wiring, not the event transport itself.
Direct queues carry actual UI actions, snapshots, patches, chat/application messages and interaction observations.
Application code should not manipulate Queue Fabric CLAIM/ACK/NACK tokens directly.
Comms ordering uses the gateway's contiguous per-access-point delivery sequence, never the manager-wide QueueWorkPackage sequence.
Subscription changes are differential; unchanged subscriptions are not torn down and rebuilt.
procedure: Server computes the desired ACTIVE/PREFETCH/ON_DEMAND subscription state.
Comms reconciles only the delta between current and desired subscriptions.
ON_DEMAND capability remains dormant until an explicit authorised request.
Live payloads continue over fixed direct queues irrespective of how their definitions were selected.

provenance.claim: Subscription/direct-queue architectural rule and module responsibilities.
Gateway delivery sequence is per access point and distinct from QueueWorkPackage sequence.
Queue Fabric direct queues carry live communications while topics carry definition-subscription delivery.
